segments.text: What was the message in French?
Le message. Very good, le message. And this was an arge word, no. So we know it's masculine, le message.
To send, to send in French is to envoy, to envoy. So how would you make envoy a French verb?
Envoy is en, v or y, and we can add our most common verb ending for French verbs onto that.
How would that sound in French, to envoy, to send?
Envoyer. That's en, v or y, envoyer. So en, em, am, am, they all sound the same in French.
They all sound like en, like emporter, to take away, like in attend, to wait, envoyer.
En, em, am, am, when they're forming a syllable, all sound the same. We have this nasal sound.
Envoyer. How would you say I have to, I must send a message? I must send a message.
Je dois envoyer un message.
I have to send you the message. I have to send you the message.
Je dois t'envoyer le message.
And the message is? Les messages.
To show in French is montrer. M-o-n-t-a-i-a, montrer.
So we have m-o, with the o-m there giving us the nasal o, and then t-r-i-a, which gives us très, très, montré.
And this is actually, this verb to show, is related to monster, even though you wouldn't believe it,
monster and demonstrate as well, demonstrate. And this is because a monster used to be like an odd animal,
an anomaly in the, in the natural world. So maybe you see a sheep with like three horns,
or something, you say, ah, that's a monster. But that sheep with three horns was also considered an omen,
a message from the gods, or the universe, or nature, or whatever.
And this is how the meaning of monster managed to come to mean show,
as we see in demonstrate and montrer. And this mon, base, as we see it in monitor and money as well,
is all about showing money, shows value, rather than having its own intrinsic value.
I must show you the messages. I must show you the messages.
Je dois te montrer les messages. How would the passage be the passage?
Le passage. Good. Deux passages of passage means passing by, deux passages. Like you could say,
I am passing by, like I'm traveling through. I am, is Je suis, Je suis, S-U-I-S, Je suis,
Je suis. I'm passing by, I am of passage. Je suis, deux passages. I'm just passing by,
I'm just traveling through. Do you remember the word, for just? Just. So I'm just passing by.
Je suis, juste, des passages. Je suis, juste, deux passages. What was I want?
Je veux. So je veux, is I want. And I don't want. I don't want, is je ne veux pas. So what's
happening here? We have ne and e for not or don't. Je ne, I not, I don't. We have
non for want. But then we also have this pas on the end, which is spelled P-A-S. Pa, P-A-S,
is related to pass, passage, passage, meaning something like step. But it has just one S
and that S is silent as we hear now. Pas, je ne veux pas. So to say I don't want in French,
we say something like I not want step. This step is kind of emphatic, no? It doesn't sound
emphatic anymore but it was probably added in the language to be emphatic, no? Miss ne
is very easily swallowed up in French. Je ne veux, je ne veux. And the modern French is often left
out. So we needed something else to hear that we were making a negative sentence. So pas,
P-A-S, step, came to be used for this. So this is the curious way in which we make the negation
in French. I want, je veux, I don't want, je ne veux pas. So we have two bits to think about
for our negation, no? How did we say you want? Tu veux, you don't want, you not want step,
you not want pass. Tu ne veux pas, tu ne veux pas. I am, what was I am?
Je suis, je suis, I am not. Je ne suis pas, je ne suis pas. I am not passing by,
like I'm not traveling through, I'm here to stay, I'm not passing by. Je ne suis pas
de passage. Je ne suis pas de passage. So be careful with de, no we have de,
not de, de passage. Very good. Je ne suis pas de passage. I am not your husband,
husband we found from le mariage. I am not your husband. Je ne suis pas ton mari. Very good.
Je ne suis pas ton mari. To eat, to eat in French is manger, manger. So we have M-A-N-G-E-R,
manger. I want to eat. Je veux manger. I don't want to eat, I don't want to eat.
What was to show related to monster? We don't have the S there.
Montré. Montré. I want to show you it. I want to show you it. In English we could say I want to
show you it, I want to show it to you. But in French we will say it this way, you eat
with you first. I want to show you it.
Je veux te le montrer. I don't want to show you it. So we don't want to think about this all
together. The first bit is I don't want. Je ne veux pas to show you it.
Te le montrer. Very good. Je ne veux pas te le montrer. Very good.
